title: רב הונא בר חייא אבוה הלוי

paragraphs: Rav Huna bar Chiyya, father of HaLevi—it should read “of Levi,” see his entry—a student of Rav. He disputes Rav Nachman in chapter Yesh Nochalin, 111a: Rav Huna bar Chiyya thought to act like Rabbi Zekharyah ben HaKatzav; Rav Nachman said to him …. I did not find in the Talmud the statement that he was Rav’s student, for his father-in-law Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba was Rav’s student. Sheerit Yosef too does not include him among Rav’s students. In Bekhorot 31a, Rav Huna bar Chiyya was needed at the time—the sages needed to ask him laws. Rabbah, Rav Yosef, and four hundred pairs of rabbis would enter before him. When he heard they were coming, he set up four hundred seats for them. They heard he had become the king’s collector, appointed to collect tax from Israel, and sent: “Let him go to his accounts”—let him pursue the distinction he chose as tax collector; we shall not go to him—“let him go to his former position.” He sent, “I retract.” Rav Yosef did not go; Rabbah went …. Yuchasin writes: Chiyya bar Huna became collector …. In Yuchasin, in Rav Sherira Gaon’s name: “We heard from our teachers that in those years after Rav Yehudah, when he did not accept the headship, Rav Huna bar Chiyya ruled in Pumbedita and had a great study house there.” (A gloss there: their words are puzzling, for Gittin says the shofar was in Rav Yehudah’s house, then Rabbah’s, then Rav Yosef’s …. Had Rav Huna bar Chiyya preceded Rabbah, it should have mentioned him.) “When he died, Rabbah bar Nachmani was compelled to accept the headship.” Rabbi Abba at Rav Huna’s doorway: Shabbat 47a. Rabbi Abba was sitting—it should read “Rabbi Abba rose to relieve himself,” as also in Ein Yaakov—and an ostrich came and swallowed Rabbi Abba’s tefillin. Rav Huna bar Chiyya rescued them. In Jerusalem Talmud, Moed Katan chapter 3, halakhah 7, Rabbi Ba caught and strangled it. Rabbi Abba said to him …; he answered, “It happened with me, and I came before Rav Mattanah and Rav Yehudah”: Moed Katan 26a. Rabbi Abba bar Binyamin bar Chiyya asked him. Rav Yosef sat behind Rav Huna bar Chiyya, and Rav Huna bar Chiyya before Rav Nachman: Bava Kamma 116b. He reported Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba, Bava Kamma 59b, who was Rav Huna bar Chiyya’s father-in-law, Bava Kamma 93. It is puzzling that in Shabbat 80b it put Rav Huna bar Chiyya’s words before Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba’s. Levi was his son; and Levi bar Shmuel repaired Rav Yehudah’s cloth. Minyomi bar Chilkiyah and Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvyah. Rav Nachman said to him, “Why did you act thus?” He answered, “For Rav Huna said ….” He said, “I shall send to Rav Huna”; he was ashamed: Bava Batra 111a. In Ulla’s name: Nedarim 56a. He reported Shmuel: Chullin 79a; Shabbat 51b; Taanit 10a. Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna may be his son.
